evidence.description: HP45 cartridge datasheet analysis and hardware reverse engineering

raw_note:
HP45 Matrix Control Mechanism:

Physical Structure:
- 300 nozzles total, arranged internally as 22×14 matrix
- Each nozzle: MOSFET switch + heating resistor (~30Ω)
- MOSFET gate → one of 22 HA address lines (HA0-HA21)
- Heater 'upper' side → one of 14 HP primitive lines (HP0-HP13)
- Heater 'lower' side → common HGND (multiple pins)

Operating Parameters:
- VDD (head supply): 9-13V (typically ~12V)
- Pulse duration: 1.5-2.0µs (typically ~1.8µs)
- Nozzle current during pulse: ~0.3-0.4A (I = V/R = 12V/30Ω)
- Only ONE HA address should be active at a time
- Multiple HP primitives can fire simultaneously (current limits permitting)

Firing Sequence (per line phase):
for address in 0..21:  # 22 address phases
    set_HA(address)              # exactly one HA line active (12V)
    hp_mask = bitmap[address]    # 14-bit mask: which HPx should fire?
    set_HP_mask(hp_mask)         # High-side MOSFETs switch 10-12V on HP lines
    wait ~1.8µs
    clear_HP_mask()
    clear_HA(address)

Sensor Pins (optional):
- 10X (C10X): Reference resistor (~300Ω)
- TSR (CTSR): Temperature-dependent resistor (~300Ω, ~11Ω per 10°C step)
- Used for temperature estimation and pulse duration adjustment
- May be ignored in minimal implementations
summary: The HP45(SI) cartridge contains 300 nozzles arranged as a 22×14 matrix with 22 address lines (HA0-HA21), 14 primitive lines (HP0-HP13), and common heater ground (HGND). Each nozzle has an internal MOSFET (gate on HAx) and heating resistor (~30Ω, on HPx line). Nozzles fire when both the HA address is active and the HP primitive receives a ~1.8µs pulse at VDD (~12V), drawing ~0.3-0.4A per nozzle.
title: HP45 Cartridge Architecture - 22×14 Nozzle Matrix Control
